subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the values of a, b if ax² + bxy + 3y² − 5x + 2y − 3 = 0 represents a circle. Also find the radius and centre.

mark_split.label: Find a and b and divide to the standard form
Find the centre and the radius

insider_note: Both conditions are needed here and each is worth stating in words: the x² and y² coefficients must match, and the xy coefficient must be zero — writing only one of them is a half answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a and b and divide to the standard form
steps.margin_note: One mark. Say both conditions. b = 0 is easy to leave out because the xy term is not printed in the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Equal x² and y² coefficients, and no xy term at all.
lines: (i) coefficient of x² = coefficient of y²
steps.why: A general second-degree equation is a circle only when the two squared terms have the same coefficient and the xy term is absent. An xy term would tilt the curve into an ellipse or a hyperbola.
common_mistakes: Giving a = 3 and stopping, without saying b = 0.
Dividing by 3 but leaving the constant as −3.

steps.label: Find the centre and the radius
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Halve the divided coefficients: g = −5/6 and f = 1/3.
steps.memory_tip: Half of −5/3 is −5/6; half of 2/3 is 1/3.
steps.why: Putting every term over 36 makes the addition one step: 25 + 4 + 36 = 65. Since 65 is not a perfect square, the radius stays as √65 over 6.
